what_it_does: This paper outlines how to build AI chips for robots that sense their environment, make decisions, and act in the real world—all without burning too much power. The core challenge: training and running large AI models that process images, sensor data, and control signals is extremely energy-intensive, making battery-powered robots impractical. The paper describes a system-level approach that combines three elements: energy-efficient AI hardware (chips optimized for common AI tasks), sensorimotor feedback loops (letting the chip read sensors and drive motors directly), and real-time control logic. Rather than running one massive AI model, this architecture moves some computation to specialized analog circuits and tightly couples AI inference with physical feedback, reducing the energy cost per decision and enabling truly autonomous robots.
